Seminar Title:

Quench-induced Cusp formation in hQCD

Seminar Type:

Department:

Speaker Name:

Jasper Singh Nongmaithem ( Rollno : 524ph6005)

Speaker Type:

MC-224

Date and Time:

27 Oct 2026 11:00 AM

Contact:

Subhash Chandra Mahapatra

Abstract:

The response of a confining flux tube to external disturbances provides a way to study nonlinear dynamics in strongly coupled gauge theories. This report examines a heavy quark&ampndashantiquark pair represented by a fundamental string in a bottom-up Einstein&ampndashdilaton background. The string endpoints undergo infinitely smooth, finite-duration displacements, after which the string evolves with fixed endpoints. Static configurations and their normal modes are calculated in the string-frame geometry, and the full Nambu&ampndashGoto equations are evolved numerically in double-null worldsheet coordinates. Preliminary results are presented for one-sided longitudinal, Z2-symmetric longitudinal, and transverse quenches. For the one-sided longitudinal calculation, cusp formation occurs later than in pure AdS under the same endpoint driving conditions. Extrapolations of the onset time also suggest a larger threshold amplitude over the pulse durations examined. The longitudinal spectrum shows increasing excitation of higher modes, consistent with the development of finer spatial structure, while stronger quench produces sharper peaks in the endpoint forces. Symmetric and transverse profiles illustrate how the direction and symmetry of the forcing change the subsequent motion. These results suggest that the confining deformation modifies the nonlinear response of the string for the configurations studied. Further work will extend the parameter space and complete the cusp, spectral, and force analyses for all three quench cases.
